g.text: The same days, sorted by the Moon: much flatter

rect.style: stroke-width: 0.00; stroke: none; fill: #0B1D2E;
stroke-width: 0.00; stroke: none; fill: #0B1D2E;

g.text: Bars: share of watched days with spawning. Pink dot: a day with spawning, larger when more tanks spawned (1–17). Open circle: a full moon. Forecast test on 1,007 complete days, Brier error: no calendar 0.136,
Moon 0.136, season 0.113, both 0.111, both plus weather 0.115. One aquarium, so this checks the field pattern and does not forecast a wild reef. Source: Sakai, Yamamoto & Maruyama (2024), reanalysed.
An aquarium in Okinawa kept a spawning diary for 1,350 days over 15 years. Predicting each year from the others, the
season cuts the error by 17%. The Moon alone cuts nothing. Tank temperature and weather add nothing.
With every day watched, the season says far more than the Moon
